sections.title: Testing Modes and Precision
body: A single test system rarely needs to handle only one kind of cell, and the Series 4000 is built around that reality with both flexible test modes and a genuinely wide precision range.

Six programmable modes cover the core of most testing protocols: Constant Current and Constant Power for standard charge and discharge cycling, Constant Voltage and Constant Resistance for specific hold or load conditions, 1 kHz AC Impedance Measurement for internal resistance characterization, and Voltage Ramp for cyclic voltammetry work. Underpinning all of these, four selectable current ranges, from a sensitive 150 µA full-scale range down to ±0.03 µA accuracy, up to a 5000 mA full-scale range, let the same system handle small research cells and larger production cells without losing measurement precision at either end. For applications needing even higher current, a single current range option extends up to 2000 A at ±0.05% full-scale accuracy.

sections.title: Available Options and Expandability
body: A test system's usefulness often depends on what it can connect to, not just what it measures on its own, and the Series 4000's option list reflects that.

Multiplexer support enables EIS integration across more channels, while telecom pulsing profiles cover GSM, CDMA, and GPRS testing scenarios. For labs working with sensor-rich test setups, thermocouple, thermistor, RTD (PT100/PT1000), pressure, reference electrode, auxiliary voltage, and pH inputs are all available, alongside digital inputs and outputs for broader lab integration. External charge and load controllers extend current handling from 5 to 200 A, and environmental chamber control, cell holders, and UPS support round out a genuinely complete test environment. Maccor also offers ongoing calibration and maintenance services to keep the system running at spec.

sections.title: Telecom Pulse Testing Explained
body: A phone battery doesn't discharge smoothly. It's hit with short, sharp current demands every time the device transmits, and that pulse behavior is exactly what telecom protocols are built to reproduce.

GSM, CDMA, and iDEN each define their own specific pulse timing and current characteristics, shaped by how those network technologies actually communicate. Testing a cell against those exact profiles, rather than a generic charge-discharge cycle, is what reveals how a battery will genuinely perform in telecom or mobile device use. The Model 4304's dedicated Pulse Testing mode, combined with its wide current range down to 300 nA, gives it the sensitivity to capture that rapid, variable current behavior accurately.
